papers.full_text: AbstractSuccessful pandemic preparedness and sustainable healthcare security increasingly rely on One Health—linking humans, animals, and the environment. Novel real-time geolocated data sources from social media, the web, digital traces, and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, combined with traditional surveillance data, are increasingly used to power AI models and enhance environmental sensing that is essential for preparedness and response in the One Health context. Despite the abundance of data streams and sensing data, the potential of AI and IoT environmental monitoring for One Health remains unfulfilled. The OHSEW (One Health Surveillance and Early Warning) framework architecture fills this gap by defining a human-centric architecture for One Health surveillance, early warning, and response, leveraging AI modelling and IoT environmental sensing, designed in particular for monitoring vector-borne diseases, zoonoses, and other environmental reservoirs of infectious diseases where the risk of spillover to human populations is high. In the OHSEW framework, we identify a rich spectrum of multiple heterogeneous data sources and a pipeline for improved surveillance, data visualisation, and training predictive AI models. These include open-source population and socioeconomic data, land use, satellite sensing, and weather forecasts, enriched by IoT environmental sensing (providing microclimate data streams) and traditional routine surveillance data reported by public health and environmental health experts. These models generate real-time data and actionable evidence for public health managers and policymakers, visualised through customisable dashboards, and provide early warning signals enabling rapid response and effective risk communication with the public. In this article, we outline the framework architecture, individual components, data pipeline, and configurable and localisable setup. To demonstrate the feasibility of the architecture, components of the OHSEW framework were piloted in real-world deployments of mosquito surveillance systems at two sites, Madeira, Portugal, and Cabedelo, Brazil. The architectures and results of these real-world deployments are presented to illustrate the feasibility of the OHSEW framework, with directions for further research outlined.Keywords: AI modelling, architecture framework, Internet of Things, One Health, vector-borne disease 4.Discussion and Future WorkIn this section, we will discuss the strengths of the framework to consider when implementing OHSEW, the key challenges to address, and opportunities for scale-up.4.1.StrengthsThe main strengths are interdisciplinarity, privacy, transparency, data standardisation and interoperability, and generalisability. Interdisciplinary The architecture will be driven by and used by public health and One Health experts, while the details of analysis, bias, and AI model training will be led by public health experts and ecologists rather than AI engineers. Through the process of adoption and localisation of the framework for their specific needs, users might prefer to tune the architecture for impact and environmental plausibility or opt for simple yet tailored solutions rather than fully generic ones with the best precision and recall. Privacy Data privacy and responsible data sharing are recommended to be built into the system and protected through open data frameworks, as defined in Layer 2, rather than treated as an afterthought (63). This is an essential matter of public trust in technology, which was severely dented after COVID-19 with the arrival of Big Tech in healthcare and governments (64). Data standardisation and interoperability Well-defined standards need to be defined and implemented in Layers 1 and 2: One Health Data and Data Integration through a Federated Architecture. Generalisability While the pilot was implemented for mosquito-borne disease surveillance, the framework and associated tools are generalisable to routine data collection for other vectors—we are currently exploring the adaptation of the digital tools for tick surveillance.Engagement with public health stakeholders builds on the collaboration from the mosquito surveillance networks. Implementing OHSEW for human disease surveillance, such as influenza or influenza-like illness (ILI), will require engagement of public health agencies, access to and sharing of reported data, and use of data provided by participatory surveillance apps such as InfluenzaNet2 (popular due to the high prevalence of the disease in the community, which was not the case for VBDs). However, the components and pipeline of the OHSEW framework will remain the same.4.2.Challenges and LimitationsIn this section, we outline key challenges to address when building AI predictive systems using the OHSEW framework, aligned with generic principles of responsible AI (39). While a detailed discussion of these principles is beyond the scope of this study, we outline a suitable governance framework and key studies to follow. Explainability AI-generated models used in the framework cannot be non-reproducible black boxes (65); they need to be sufficiently transparent and interpretable to be trusted to support scientific learning and decision-making (42). Surveillance ethics and data abuse Ethical challenges for AI in public health surveillance have been well understood (39). These include concerns over the access to and use of citizens’ private data, such as phone mobility data (e.g., COVID-19 proximity tracking), due to the danger of disproportionate surveillance, policy measures for enforcement of compliance, unfair false positives, and documented data misuse (39, 66). However, data ownership and data access in public health (67) are societal challenges that we are currently grappling with, rather than being exclusive to One Health (68). Noise and misinformation Noise from digital data sources, fake accounts, and trolls on social media can exacerbate misinformation, making the extraction of meaningful information increasingly challenging (69). Prudence with incorporating social media (especially X) is recommended. Methods for filtering low-quality, biased news and misinformation are also recommended, as shown by an analysis of Twitter during COVID-19 (70) and around HPV vaccine misinformation (71, 72). These studies demonstrated that misinformation often originates from a small number of accounts and sources. Another major challenge for public health agencies when relying on data collected by IT providers and AI companies, rather than the bespoke tools recommended by OHSEW, is the poorly regulated role of Big Tech in health, with these companies dominating social media platforms with unprecedented political influence, gatekeeping public narratives, and having private access to healthcare systems data such as that of the NHS. OHSEW recommends building bespoke apps and tools for data collection to avoid challenges associated with open and public data sources.These issues lead to the need for data and AI Sovereignty for Europe and other nations to reduce the overreliance on the US tech sector—for data control, AI governance, and ownership. As Europe is emerging as an important player, principles have been proposed for responsible One Health systems (73). Bias Bias in data used for training AI models is well described. This is of particular importance in One Health systems, where inequitable data collection is an inevitable outcome of the lack of resources and access in less-resourced parts of the world (74). Equitable Data Partnerships across the Global North and South are of intrinsic importance—between public health and animal health experts, ecologists, and those affected—humans, animals, farmers, and environmentalists—as well as international stakeholders. These principles are essential for interoperability in OHSEW systems integrating veterinary, medical, and environmental systems through federated architectures.In general, more robust ethical governance for AI models is required, relying on clarifying core ethical principles from the outset of development while empowering citizens and stakeholders to participate in collaborative governance frameworks supporting ethics-by-design methodologies for systems using AI to be equitable and safe beyond One Health (75).4.3.Effective Deployment and Future WorkIn order to effectively deploy the OHSEW architecture in any context, national investment in infrastructure, routine surveillance, and capacity building is essential.Furthermore, safe data-sharing platforms are required. In Europe, the open health data paradigm is supported through the European Health Data Space (EHDS) (76). EHDS establishes common standards for health data quality, interoperability, and cross-border access, and, as a result, should enable AI model training on diverse data from European populations, improving fairness. EHDS also includes provisions for secondary data use in research while maintaining strong safeguards. EHDS provides a new opportunity for One Health systems.In terms of AI responsibility and safety, the use of AI models developed and trained for specific diseases by researchers at the national level might be the natural choice. If industry models are considered by national governments, their governance might be a challenge, as the recent WHO report highlighted (77). Even in the European region, only 8% of MSs have an AI vision and health strategy; AI literacy is lagging behind technological developments, and EHDS readiness remains low (only 30% have guidance on the secondary use of health data and cross-border sharing) (78).Another challenge lies in the intrinsically collaborative nature of public health and One Health and the need for the implementation of data standards and interoperability, as highlighted in OHSEW Layer 2: Data Integration through a Federated Architecture. This is much more challenging in public health and One Health settings than in primary and clinical care, which is a national responsibility and where data standards are normally well regulated (79). One Health relies on multiple international organisations to work together and agree on standards, data sharing, model training, and coordinating response.Our current efforts and future research include further recommenders on the selection of One Health data streams for various diseases (Layer 1), standards and protocols (Layer 2), selection of models (Layer 3), and definitions of components for the dashboard (Layer 4). 5.ConclusionPandemic preparedness and global health security rely on One Health—the interaction among humans, animals, and the environment. However, leveraging the abundance of real-time, geolocated data sources and developing bespoke apps and digital tools for AI predictive modelling and IoT environmental monitoring, trained and calibrated by routine surveillance data for One Health needs, remain unfulfilled.In this study, we presented the OHSEW framework—a human-centric architecture for One Health surveillance, early warning, and response leveraging heterogeneous data sources for AI modelling and IoT environmental monitoring, championing the development and deployment of bespoke mobile tools and IoT sensor sets to fill the gap in missing fine-grained, real-time, GPS-enabled surveillance datasets, particularly much-needed ones in LMICs. full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractSuccessful pandemic preparedness and sustainable healthcare security increasingly rely on One Health—linking humans, animals, and the environment. Novel real-time geolocated data sources from social media, the web, digital traces, and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, combined with traditional surveillance data, are increasingly used to power AI models and enhance environmental sensing that is essential for preparedness and response in the One Health context. Despite the abundance of data streams and sensing data, the potential of AI and IoT environmental monitoring for One Health remains unfulfilled. The OHSEW (One Health Surveillance and Early Warning) framework architecture fills this gap by defining a human-centric architecture for One Health surveillance, early warning, and response, leveraging AI modelling and IoT environmental sensing, designed in particular for monitoring vector-borne diseases, zoonoses, and other environmental reservoirs of infectious diseases where the risk of spillover to human populations is high. In the OHSEW framework, we identify a rich spectrum of multiple heterogeneous data sources and a pipeline for improved surveillance, data visualisation, and training predictive AI models. These include open-source population and socioeconomic data, land use, satellite sensing, and weather forecasts, enriched by IoT environmental sensing (providing microclimate data streams) and traditional routine surveillance data reported by public health and environmental health experts. These models generate real-time data and actionable evidence for public health managers and policymakers, visualised through customisable dashboards, and provide early warning signals enabling rapid response and effective risk communication with the public. In this article, we outline the framework architecture, individual components, data pipeline, and configurable and localisable setup. To demonstrate the feasibility of the architecture, components of the OHSEW framework were piloted in real-world deployments of mosquito surveillance systems at two sites, Madeira, Portugal, and Cabedelo, Brazil. The architectures and results of these real-world deployments are presented to illustrate the feasibility of the OHSEW framework, with directions for further research outlined.Keywords: AI modelling, architecture framework, Internet of Things, One Health, vector-borne disease
full_text_sections.discussion: 4.Discussion and Future WorkIn this section, we will discuss the strengths of the framework to consider when implementing OHSEW, the key challenges to address, and opportunities for scale-up.4.1.StrengthsThe main strengths are interdisciplinarity, privacy, transparency, data standardisation and interoperability, and generalisability. Interdisciplinary The architecture will be driven by and used by public health and One Health experts, while the details of analysis, bias, and AI model training will be led by public health experts and ecologists rather than AI engineers. Through the process of adoption and localisation of the framework for their specific needs, users might prefer to tune the architecture for impact and environmental plausibility or opt for simple yet tailored solutions rather than fully generic ones with the best precision and recall. Privacy Data privacy and responsible data sharing are recommended to be built into the system and protected through open data frameworks, as defined in Layer 2, rather than treated as an afterthought (63). This is an essential matter of public trust in technology, which was severely dented after COVID-19 with the arrival of Big Tech in healthcare and governments (64). Data standardisation and interoperability Well-defined standards need to be defined and implemented in Layers 1 and 2: One Health Data and Data Integration through a Federated Architecture. Generalisability While the pilot was implemented for mosquito-borne disease surveillance, the framework and associated tools are generalisable to routine data collection for other vectors—we are currently exploring the adaptation of the digital tools for tick surveillance.Engagement with public health stakeholders builds on the collaboration from the mosquito surveillance networks. Implementing OHSEW for human disease surveillance, such as influenza or influenza-like illness (ILI), will require engagement of public health agencies, access to and sharing of reported data, and use of data provided by participatory surveillance apps such as InfluenzaNet2 (popular due to the high prevalence of the disease in the community, which was not the case for VBDs). However, the components and pipeline of the OHSEW framework will remain the same.4.2.Challenges and LimitationsIn this section, we outline key challenges to address when building AI predictive systems using the OHSEW framework, aligned with generic principles of responsible AI (39). While a detailed discussion of these principles is beyond the scope of this study, we outline a suitable governance framework and key studies to follow. Explainability AI-generated models used in the framework cannot be non-reproducible black boxes (65); they need to be sufficiently transparent and interpretable to be trusted to support scientific learning and decision-making (42). Surveillance ethics and data abuse Ethical challenges for AI in public health surveillance have been well understood (39). These include concerns over the access to and use of citizens’ private data, such as phone mobility data (e.g., COVID-19 proximity tracking), due to the danger of disproportionate surveillance, policy measures for enforcement of compliance, unfair false positives, and documented data misuse (39, 66). However, data ownership and data access in public health (67) are societal challenges that we are currently grappling with, rather than being exclusive to One Health (68). Noise and misinformation Noise from digital data sources, fake accounts, and trolls on social media can exacerbate misinformation, making the extraction of meaningful information increasingly challenging (69). Prudence with incorporating social media (especially X) is recommended. Methods for filtering low-quality, biased news and misinformation are also recommended, as shown by an analysis of Twitter during COVID-19 (70) and around HPV vaccine misinformation (71, 72). These studies demonstrated that misinformation often originates from a small number of accounts and sources. Another major challenge for public health agencies when relying on data collected by IT providers and AI companies, rather than the bespoke tools recommended by OHSEW, is the poorly regulated role of Big Tech in health, with these companies dominating social media platforms with unprecedented political influence, gatekeeping public narratives, and having private access to healthcare systems data such as that of the NHS. OHSEW recommends building bespoke apps and tools for data collection to avoid challenges associated with open and public data sources.These issues lead to the need for data and AI Sovereignty for Europe and other nations to reduce the overreliance on the US tech sector—for data control, AI governance, and ownership. As Europe is emerging as an important player, principles have been proposed for responsible One Health systems (73). Bias Bias in data used for training AI models is well described. This is of particular importance in One Health systems, where inequitable data collection is an inevitable outcome of the lack of resources and access in less-resourced parts of the world (74). Equitable Data Partnerships across the Global North and South are of intrinsic importance—between public health and animal health experts, ecologists, and those affected—humans, animals, farmers, and environmentalists—as well as international stakeholders. These principles are essential for interoperability in OHSEW systems integrating veterinary, medical, and environmental systems through federated architectures.In general, more robust ethical governance for AI models is required, relying on clarifying core ethical principles from the outset of development while empowering citizens and stakeholders to participate in collaborative governance frameworks supporting ethics-by-design methodologies for systems using AI to be equitable and safe beyond One Health (75).4.3.Effective Deployment and Future WorkIn order to effectively deploy the OHSEW architecture in any context, national investment in infrastructure, routine surveillance, and capacity building is essential.Furthermore, safe data-sharing platforms are required. In Europe, the open health data paradigm is supported through the European Health Data Space (EHDS) (76). EHDS establishes common standards for health data quality, interoperability, and cross-border access, and, as a result, should enable AI model training on diverse data from European populations, improving fairness. EHDS also includes provisions for secondary data use in research while maintaining strong safeguards. EHDS provides a new opportunity for One Health systems.In terms of AI responsibility and safety, the use of AI models developed and trained for specific diseases by researchers at the national level might be the natural choice. If industry models are considered by national governments, their governance might be a challenge, as the recent WHO report highlighted (77). Even in the European region, only 8% of MSs have an AI vision and health strategy; AI literacy is lagging behind technological developments, and EHDS readiness remains low (only 30% have guidance on the secondary use of health data and cross-border sharing) (78).Another challenge lies in the intrinsically collaborative nature of public health and One Health and the need for the implementation of data standards and interoperability, as highlighted in OHSEW Layer 2: Data Integration through a Federated Architecture. This is much more challenging in public health and One Health settings than in primary and clinical care, which is a national responsibility and where data standards are normally well regulated (79). analysis.summary_en: This study presents an interdisciplinary human-centric architectural framework for One Health surveillance, early warning, and response, leveraging AI modelling and IoT environmental monitoring. The framework's feasibility was demonstrated through a real-world pilot for mosquito-borne disease surveillance in Brazil and Madeira over two years, showing increased dengue, chikungunya, and malaria cases. The architecture includes six layers for data integration and early warning, emphasizing the importance of equitable data partnerships and ethical governance for AI models. elements_zh.main_results: 输入性登革热病例从2023年的631例增加到2024年的904例,同时基孔肯雅热和疟疾病例也有所增加。分析人类、动物和废水等环境来源的基因组数据的人工智能模型已经证明了早期预警和加强抗菌药物管理 (AMS) 的潜力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些实际部署的架构和结果旨在说明 OHSEW 框架的可行性,并概述了进一步研究的方向。One Health 是检测现有传染病 暴发 和潜在 跨物种溢出(跨物种 暴发)以及识别人际 暴发 环境(下一次大流行最有可能爆发)的驱动方法。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop an interdisciplinary human-centric architectural framework for One Health surveillance, early warning, and response, leveraging AI modelling and IoT environmental monitoring. This is of particular importance in One Health systems, where inequitable data collection is an inevitable outcome of the lack of resources and access in less-resourced parts of the world.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved a real-world pilot for mosquito-borne disease surveillance deployed with users in Brazil and Madeira over 2 years. These studies demonstrated that misinformation often originates from a small number of accounts and sources.
analysis_en.methods: Methods for filtering low-quality, biased news and misinformation are also recommended, as shown by an analysis of Twitter during COVID-19 and around HPV vaccine misinformation. The architecture consists of six layers implementing the data pipeline, including One Health Data Sources, Data Integration through a Federated Architecture, Spatiotemporal and AI Modelling for Early Warning, and Component-based Configurable Dashboards for decision-makers.
analysis_en.main_results: Imported dengue cases increased from 631 in 2023 to 904 in 2024, while chikungunya and malaria cases also increased. AI models analysing genomic data from humans, animals, and environmental sources, such as wastewater, have demonstrated the potential for early warning and strengthening antimicrobial stewardship (AMS).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The architectures and results of these real-world deployments are presented to illustrate the feasibility of the OHSEW framework, with directions for further research outlined. One Health is the driving approach for detecting outbreaks of existing communicable diseases and potential spillovers (cross-species outbreaks) and for identifying settings of human-to-human transmission–the most likely onset of the next pandemic.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Implementing OHSEW for human disease surveillance, such as influenza or influenza-like illness (ILI), will require engagement of public health agencies, access to and sharing of reported data, and use of data provided by participatory surveillance apps such as InfluenzaNet2.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Generalisability While the pilot was implemented for mosquito-borne disease surveillance, the framework and associated tools are generalisable to routine data collection for other vectors—we are currently exploring the adaptation of the digital tools for tick surveillance. The supplied evidence does not report specific numerical findings or statistical analyses.

papers.full_text: TEMPORAL PATTERNS IN REPORTED DENGUE CASES (2020-2025) AND DENGUE-RELATED KNOWLEDGE, ATTITUDES, AND PRACTICES AMONG PRIMARY HEALTHCARE CENTER ATTENDEES IN JAZAN, SAUDI ARABIA Abstract Dengue remains a major public-health concern in southwestern Saudi Arabia, where local surveillance and community prevention are both essential. This study used the combination of retrospective surveillance and cross-sectional Knowledge, Attitude and Practices (KAP) assessment in Jazan Region. The number of laboratory confirmed dengue cases reported via the Saudi Ministry of Health HESN Plus system from 2020 until 2025 was included in Component A. There were 430 adult primary healthcare (PHC) visitors who answered the structured KAP questionnaire in component B. Case counts were totaled and inter-year comparisons were made; KAP data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, nonparametric tests, Spearman correlations, reliability analysis, and multiple linear regression. Confirmed cases varied markedly across the study period: 33 in 2020, 24 in 2021, 177 in 2022, 270 in 2023, 452 in 2024, and 32 in 2025. The distribution of the number of counts across the year was not equal (χ2(5, N=988) = 902.01, p<.001), but annual population-based incidence rates were not possible as there were no denominators available. Among PHC visitors, mean standardized knowledge, attitude, practice, and total KAP scores were 83.69, 75.40, 87.55, and 82.21, respectively; 68.8%, 54.2%, 79.8%, and 79.1% met the study-defined 75% thresholds. There were important gaps of knowledge in recognition of Aedes, knowledge of the biting time and knowledge of inspecting larvae along with community participation. In adjusted models, sex and income were shown to be associated with KAP outcomes, and history of dengue was shown to be positively associated with total KAP. papers.title_original: TEMPORAL PATTERNS IN REPORTED DENGUE CASES (2020-2025) AND DENGUE-RELATED KNOWLEDGE, ATTITUDES, AND PRACTICES AMONG PRIMARY HEALTHCARE CENTER ATTENDEES IN JAZAN, SAUDI ARABIA

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate temporal patterns in reported dengue cases and dengue-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices among primary healthcare center attendees in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, to address the public-health concern of dengue in the region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study combined retrospective surveillance of dengue cases and a cross-sectional Knowledge, Attitude, and Practices (KAP) assessment conducted among primary healthcare center attendees in Jazan, Saudi Arabia. It included 430 adults who completed a structured KAP questionnaire.
analysis.methods: Case counts were aggregated and compared across years; KAP data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, nonparametric tests, Spearman correlations, reliability analysis, and multiple linear regression.
analysis.main_results: The number of laboratory-confirmed dengue cases varied significantly across the study period, with 33 in 2020, 24 in 2021, 177 in 2023, 452 in 2024, and 32 in 2025. Among PHC attendees, mean knowledge, attitude, practice, and total KAP scores were 83.69, 75.40, 87.55, and 82.21, respectively, with 68.8%, 54.2%, 79.8%, and 79.1% meeting the 75% threshold.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the fluctuating nature of dengue cases and the need for improved community awareness and engagement, as well as the association between demographic factors and KAP outcomes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results support the importance of continued monitoring and targeted vector literacy programs in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, to enhance community prevention efforts and reduce dengue transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study lacked annual population-based incidence rates due to the absence of denominators, and the KAP survey was limited to PHC attendees, potentially affecting generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined temporal patterns in reported dengue cases and dengue-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices among primary healthcare center attendees in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, from 2020 to 2025. It combined retrospective surveillance with a cross-sectional KAP assessment, revealing significant fluctuations in case numbers and varying levels of community awareness. The analysis used descriptive statistics, nonparametric tests, and regression models to evaluate KAP scores, which showed gaps in knowledge about Aedes mosquitoes and prevention practices. The study suggests that targeted vector literacy and community engagement are essential to address these gaps and reduce dengue transmission. However, the lack of population denominators and limited sample scope may affect the generalizability of the findings, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查沙特阿拉伯朱宰恩地区初级卫生保健中心就诊者中登革热病例报告的时间模式及其相关知识、态度和行为,以应对该地区登革热的公共卫生问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究结合了登革热病例的回顾性监测和沙特阿拉伯朱宰恩地区初级卫生保健中心就诊者中进行的横断面知识、态度和行为(KAP)评估。研究纳入了430名完成结构化KAP问卷的成年人。
elements_zh.methods: 病例数量按年份汇总并进行比较;KAP数据通过描述性统计、非参数检验、斯皮尔曼相关性、可靠性分析和多元线性回归进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: The number of laboratory-confirmed dengue cases varied significantly across the study period, with 33 in 2020, 24 in 2021, 177 in 2023, 452 in 2024, and 32 in 2025. Among PHC attendees, mean knowledge, attitude, practice, and total KAP scores were 83.69, 75.40, 87.55, and 82.21, respectively, with 68.8%, 54.2%, 79.8%, and 79.1% meeting the 75% threshold.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果突显了登革热病例波动的特性,并强调了提高社区意识和参与的必要性,以及人口学因素与KAP结果之间的关联。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持在沙特阿拉伯朱宰恩地区持续监测和针对性的媒介知识普及项目的重要性,以增强社区预防措施并减少登革热传播。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于缺乏分母,本研究未能获得年度基于人口的发病率率,且KAP调查仅限于PHC就诊者,可能影响结果的普遍适用性。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

Search Search Home News PAHO calls for strengthened surveillance and preparedness amid increases in dengue and chikungunya in the Americas PAHO calls for strengthened surveillance and preparedness amid increases in dengue and chikungunya in the Americas Copied to clipboard The Organization highlights recent increases in dengue cases in several countries and the resurgence of chikungunya transmission in areas where the virus had not circulated for several years, as South America approaches its peak transmission season. Washington, D.C., October 21, 2026 (PAHO) – The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) called on countries in the Americas to strengthen surveillance and prepare health services in response to recent increases in dengue observed in several countries and increased and renewed chikungunya transmission in countries and territories where viral circulation had not been documented for several years. The call comes amid the anticipated intensification of the El Niño phenomenon and as South America approaches the peak transmission season for these diseases. In an epidemiological update published on October 20, PAHO reported that as of mid-September, 1.69 million suspected dengue cases had been reported in the Region, including 3,413 severe cases and 571 deaths. Although the cumulative number of reported cases represents a 58% decrease compared with the same period in 2025, this decline has not been uniform across the Region: increases have been observed in recent weeks in countries in the Andean, Central American, and Caribbean subregions. Circulation of all four dengue virus serotypes has also been identified in the Americas in 2026. PAHO also highlighted the chikungunya situation, with transmission increasing between late 2025 and 2026 and reemerging in countries and territories that had not documented viral circulation for several years. As of mid-September, 213,919 suspected cases had been reported, of which 78,481 were confirmed, along with 88 deaths in 20 countries in the Region. The update also points to transmission in new areas, outbreaks outside historical transmission seasons, longer transmission periods, and increased reporting of more severe clinical manifestations. Strengthening prevention and preparing health services In response, PAHO urged countries to strengthen epidemiological, virological, and entomological surveillance, increase diagnostic capacity, and ensure early detection and timely clinical management of cases. The Organization also recommended stepping up integrated measures to control Aedes mosquitoes, the main vectors of these diseases. PAHO recommends that health services prepare to respond to potential increases in cases at all levels of care, with particular emphasis on strengthening primary health care capacity to recognize dengue warning signs early and prevent progression to severe disease. Hospitals should also be prepared to manage cases with dengue warning signs and severe cases of these diseases. Eliminating mosquito breeding sites remains a key measure to reduce mosquito populations. PAHO recommends strengthening environmental management, eliminating containers that collect water, and promoting the active participation of communities, families, local authorities, and other sectors in prevention and control efforts. elements_zh.event: PAHO呼吁加强流行病学监测和应对能力,以应对美洲地区近期登革热和寨卡病毒病例的增加。该组织指出寨卡病毒在一些多年未见的地区重新出现,并注意到厄尔尼诺现象预计的加剧以及寨卡病毒季节高峰的到来。
elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: As of mid-September 2026, 1.69 million suspected dengue cases were reported, including 3,413 severe cases and 571 deaths. Chikungunya transmission has increased, with 213,919 suspected cases and 88 deaths in 20 countries. The update also notes transmission in new areas, outbreaks outside historical seasons, and longer transmission periods.
elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: PAHO敦促各国加强流行病学监测,提高诊断能力,并为潜在病例增加做好卫生服务准备。该组织建议采取综合蚊虫控制措施、环境管理以及社区参与预防和控制工作。

analysis_en.time: PAHO reported the epidemiological update on October 20, 2026, with the event date being mid-September 2026. The call for strengthened surveillance comes as South America approaches its peak transmission season, which is anticipated to intensify due to the El Niño phenomenon.
analysis_en.location_and_population: The Americas, with specific mention of South America, the Andean, Central American, and Caribbean subregions. The affected population includes countries and territories in the Region, with a focus on areas where dengue and chikungunya transmission has increased.
analysis_en.event: PAHO called for strengthened surveillance and preparedness in response to recent increases in dengue and chikungunya cases in the Americas. The organization highlighted the resurgence of chikungunya in areas where it had not circulated for several years, and noted the anticipated intensification of the El Niño phenomenon and peak transmission season.
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: As of mid-September 2026, 1.69 million suspected dengue cases were reported, including 3,413 severe cases and 571 deaths. Chikungunya transmission has increased, with 213,919 suspected cases and 88 deaths in 20 countries. The update also notes transmission in new areas, outbreaks outside historical seasons, and longer transmission periods.
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: PAHO urged countries to strengthen surveillance, increase diagnostic capacity, and prepare health services for potential increases in cases. The organization recommended integrated mosquito control measures, environmental management, and community participation in prevention and control efforts.

news.title_zh: 美洲卫生组织呼吁加强流行病学监测和应对能力,应对美洲地区登革热和寨卡病毒病例增加
news.source_body_en: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has called for enhanced surveillance and preparedness in the Americas amid rising dengue and chikungunya cases. As of mid-September 2026, 1.69 million suspected dengue cases were reported, including 3,413 severe cases and 571 deaths, with increases observed in the Andean, Central American, and Caribbean subregions. Chikungunya transmission has also surged, with 213,919 suspected cases and 88 deaths in 20 countries. PAHO attributes these trends to the anticipated intensification of the El Niño phenomenon and the peak transmission season in South America. The organization recommends strengthening epidemiological, virological, and entomological surveillance, increasing diagnostic capacity, and preparing health services to manage potential case surges. Integrated mosquito control measures, including eliminating breeding sites and community engagement, are emphasized to mitigate the spread of these diseases.

analysis.time: The PAHO notice was published on 21 Oct 2026, and the call for strengthened surveillance and preparedness was reported on the same date.

analysis.event: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), represented by Director Jarbas Barbosa, issued a public call for enhanced surveillance and preparedness in response to reported increases in dengue and chikungunya. news.title_zh: 美洲卫生组织呼吁加强监测和应对能力,应对美洲地区登革热和寨卡病毒活动增加 - 美洲卫生组织(PAHO)
news.source_body_en: On 21 October 2026, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) issued an official alert highlighting rising dengue and chikungunya activity across the Americas. Director Jarbas Barbosa called on member states to boost surveillance and preparedness to better detect and respond to these arboviral threats. While the announcement confirms that case numbers are climbing, it does not provide specific counts of infections, deaths, or affected communities. The guidance focuses on strengthening regional early‐warning systems and public‐health readiness, but details of investigations, testing, or control measures are not included, leaving the precise scale and risk level uncertain. This statement reflects PAHO’s role in coordinating health responses in the region and underscores the need for continued monitoring of dengue and chikungunya trends.
news.content_zh: 2026年10月21日,美洲卫生组织(PAHO)发布了一项官方警报,指出美洲地区登革热和寨卡病毒活动正在上升。主任Jarbas Barbosa呼吁成员国加强监测和应对能力,以更好地检测和应对这些虫媒病毒威胁。尽管该声明确认了病例数量在上升,但并未提供具体的感染人数、死亡人数或受影响社区的具体数据。该指导重点在于加强区域早期预警系统和公共卫生应对能力,但未包含调查、检测或控制措施的细节,因此疫情的确切规模和风险水平仍不确定。该声明反映了美洲卫生组织在该地区协调卫生应对措施的作用,并强调了继续监测登革热和寨卡病毒趋势的必要性。

Search|t Updates Countries Disasters Organizations Topics Jobs Training Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA World + 15 more Epidemic and emerging disease alerts in the Pacific as of 20 October 2026 Format Map Source SPC Posted 20 Oct 2026 Originally published 20 Oct 2026 Attachments Download Map (PDF | 534.32 KB | 2 pages) Highlights/updates since the last map was sent on PacNet on 13 October 2026: Dengue • Marshall Islands: The 15th Outbreak Situation Reports on dengue in Majuro and Ebeye covering 15 August to 15 October, record 501 specimens tested (Majuro 411, Ebeye 90) and 156 positive cases, confirmed and probable (Majuro 124, Ebeye 32). This is an increase of 21 cases from the 137 cases reported on 05 October (12th Outbreak Situation Reports). The positivity has fallen to 30% in Majuro and 36% in Ebeye. No deaths have been reported. Cumulative hospitalisations rose to thirteen. The attack rate is 5.4 per 1,000 in Majuro and 3.3 per 1,000 in Ebeye. Only DENV-1 has been detected. Vector control has been completed at the households of positive cases, 26 schools and 60 churches have been sprayed, and surveillance is being strengthened on the neighbouring islands. On 08 October 2026, the Cabinet declared a state of disaster for El Niño and the dengue outbreak. The red alert for dengue (DENV-1) remains in effect. – Source: Republic of the Marshall Islands Ministry of Health and Human Services, Outbreak of Dengue Fever Cases in Majuro & Ebeye, 13th, 14th and 15th Outbreak Situation Reports shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 19 October 2026. • Samoa: Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report Issue No. 77, covering EpiWeek 40 (28 September to 04 October 2026), reports 64 new cases, up 73% on the previous week, with one laboratory-confirmed case and three new admissions. No new intensive care admission and no death were reported. Since 01 January 2025, 20,374 clinically diagnosed cases, 5,547 laboratory-confirmed cases and nine dengue-related deaths have been recorded. DENV-1 accounts for 52% and DENV-2 for 48% of serotyped cases, and children under 15 years for 73% of cases. The blue alert for dengue (DENV-1 & DENV-2) remains in effect. – Source: Ministry of Health Samoa, Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report Issue No. 77 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 16 October 2026. • Vanuatu: On 15 October 2026, the Ministry of Health declared a dengue outbreak on Malekula Island, Malampa Province, after four dengue cases were reported between 02 and 12 October in the Central North East and North Malekula Area Councils, with evidence of local transmission. Malekula is the fourth island with a declared outbreak, after Efate, Santo and Tanna. The same day, Malampa Provincial Health reported 22 dengue cases on Malekula, including six laboratory-confirmed, in North East and Central Malekula, with no deaths and no hospitalisations. Surveillance, case investigation, mosquito control and community awareness are being strengthened, and free dengue testing is offered at Norsup Hospital. The red alert for dengue (DENV-1) remains in effect for Vanuatu. – Sources: Vanuatu Ministry of Health, Dengue outbreak declared on Malekula Island, accessed on 20 October 2026 and Malampa Provincial Health, Dengue fever i stap long Malampa, accessed on 20 October 2026. Measles • Papua New Guinea: The National Department of Health weekly bulletin for EpiWeek 41 (05 to 11 October 2026) has changed the measles case count: cases are now counted as confirmed by the Expert Review Group instead of laboratory IgM-positive results. On this basis, three confirmed measles cases have been reported in 2026 (East Sepik 2, New Ireland 1), against 17 laboratory-confirmed cases reported up to EpiWeek 40. The last onset date remains 15 September 2026. The measles-rubella vaccination campaign continues to target all children under seven in every district with a detected measles or rubella case. The red alert for measles remains in effect for Papua New Guinea. – Source: Papua New Guinea National Department of Health, Public Health Events Weekly Bulletin, EpiWeek 41, shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 15 October 2026. Respiratory diseases • New Caledonia: The Department of Health and Social Affairs (DASS) influenza bulletin 2026-#10 of 16 October 2026 reports that the epidemic continues, with circulation still intense but levelling off: 130 laboratory-confirmed cases in EpiWeek 41 (05 to 11 October), against 151 in week 40. It is the first decrease since the start of the epidemic, and test positivity fell from 65% to 55%. A(H1N1)pdm09 remains largely predominant (98 of 130, the other 32 influenza A not subtyped). Hospital impact remains significant, with 67 patients hospitalised in EpiWeek 41 (median age 68 years), and intensive care bed occupancy has exceeded 80% on 8 of the last 14 days. Emergency department activity has stabilised at a high level (1,832 presentations in EpiWeek 41, against an average of 1,300), and acute respiratory infections accounted for 13% of presentations, mainly influenza. The red alert for influenza A remains in effect for New Caledonia. – Source: Direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales de Nouvelle-Calédonie, Vigilance DASS bulletin 2026-#10, influenza epidemic shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 16 October 2026. • New Zealand: For the week ending 11 October 2026, the all-cause SARI hospitalisation rate in the Auckland region decreased again and remains in the low activity band. Influenza remained the most commonly detected virus among SARI patients, and SARI influenza test positivity rose from 18.6 to 25.9%, while positivity among sentinel GP influenza-like illness cases fell slightly from 17.6 to 15.8%. Pacific peoples have had the highest cumulative rates of influenza-, RSV- and SARS-CoV-2-positive SARI hospitalisation in 2026. The blue alert for influenza A remains in effect for New Zealand. – Source: PHF Science, New Zealand Acute Respiratory Illness dashboard, accessed on 20 October 2026. • Tonga: The weekly syndromic surveillance report for EpiWeek 41 (05 to 11 October 2026) records 137 influenza-like illness cases, against 99 in week 40, the seventh consecutive weekly increase and the highest weekly count of 2026, and severe acute respiratory infections rose from 14 to 20, above the alert threshold. Between 03 August and 11 October, 156 of 336 tested ILI cases (46.4%) were positive for influenza A, against 89 a week earlier, and 67 SARI patients were hospitalised. The number of deaths among SARI cases is unchanged at three, two of them laboratory-confirmed influenza A. A red alert for influenza A is issued for Tonga. – Source: Tonga Ministry of Health, Weekly Communicable Diseases Syndromic Surveillance, EpiWeek 41 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 20 October 2026. Rotavirus • Federated States of Micronesia: The Yap weekly bulletin for EpiWeek 41 (05 to 11 October 2026) shows diarrhoea on alert for an eighth consecutive week, although cases decreased to 9 from 16 in EpiWeek 40, still above the alert threshold of 7. Of four patients tested with a gastrointestinal multiplex PCR panel, three were positive: one adenovirus and EPEC co-infection, one EAEC and one rotavirus A. Among 100 diarrhoea cases in children aged 0 to 5 years this season, 34 had completed rotavirus vaccination. A public health advisory on diarrhoeal illness remains in place. The blue alert for rotavirus remains in effect for the Federated States of Micronesia (Yap State). – Source: Yap State Department of Health Services, Communicable Disease Weekly Bulletin, EpiWeek 41 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 14 October 2026. Other Information: Chikungunya • New Zealand: In surveillance week 41 (10 to 16 October 2026), one confirmed chikungunya case was notified in New Zealand in a person who had been to the Cook Islands during the incubation period. Year to date, four confirmed chikungunya cases (Cook Islands 1, Indonesia 2, Sri Lanka 1) and two probable cases have been notified, all with overseas exposure. – Source: PHF Science, NZ Arbovirus Notifications by Country, week 41 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 19 October 2026. Dengue • Hawai’i: On 13 October 2026, the Hawaiʻi Department of Health reported a new travel-related dengue case on Oʻahu, in a person exposed while travelling in a region where dengue is common. It is the ninth dengue case reported in Hawaiʻi in 2026. No link to previous cases has been found, mosquito inspection and control were carried out around the affected area, and the risk of local transmission is considered low. – Source: Hawaiʻi Department of Health, DOH reports another travel-related dengue virus case, accessed on 20 October 2026. One Health - High pathogenicity avian influenza • Australia: The national H5 bird flu dashboard recorded 713 confirmed events in wildlife as of 16 October 2026, against 700 on 09 October: South Australia 331, Victoria 245, New South Wales 71, Tasmania 53, Western Australia 10, Queensland 2 and Jervis Bay Territory 1. H5 has not been reported from any Pacific Island country or territory to date. – Sources: Australian Government Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry, H5 bird flu latest data accessed on 20 October 2026. Respiratory diseases • French Polynesia: The health surveillance bulletin no. 37, covering data to EpiWeek 41 (05 to 11 October 2026), reports 10 influenza A cases in EpiWeek 41, against four in EpiWeek 40, three subtyped A(H1N1)pdm09 and three A(H3N2). Five patients were hospitalised, one of them in intensive care. Influenza waves in French Polynesia usually follow the Northern Hemisphere, between October and April. The 2025-2026 wave caused 200 hospitalisations, 23 intensive care admissions and 13 deaths. The influenza vaccination campaign will start on 26 October 2026. – Source: Agence de régulation de l'action sanitaire et sociale (ARASS), Bulletin de Surveillance Sanitaire de Polynésie française n°37 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 20 October 2026. Latest Updates Yemen GBV emergency referral pathways Oct 2026 Spain + 2 more Spain, France, Italy | Storm Adam - DG ECHO Daily Map | 21/10/2026 Haiti IMAWG Haïti : Compte rendu de réunion, en ligne, 21 octobre 2026 [Meeting Minutes] DR Congo TDRs Comité Provincial de Coordination de la Réponse Éducative en Contexte de Maladie à Virus Ebola (MVE 17)_ ITURI, Oct 2026

analysis.brief_en: Dengue virus outbreaks and related disease alerts were reported in several Pacific countries as of 20 October 2026. In the Marshall Islands, 156 positive cases were recorded, with 501 specimens tested. Samoa reported 64 new cases, while Vanuatu declared a dengue outbreak on Malekula Island. Tonga saw 137 influenza-like illness cases, with 67 SARI patients hospitalized. Vector control and surveillance measures are ongoing in affected areas.

In the Marshall Islands, 156 positive cases were recorded, with 501 specimens tested. Samoa reported 64 new cases, while Vanuatu declared a dengue outbreak on Malekula Island. Tonga saw 137 influenza-like illness cases, with 67 SARI patients hospitalized. Vector control and surveillance measures are ongoing in affected areas.

news.source_body_en: Dengue virus outbreaks and related disease alerts were reported in several Pacific countries as of 20 October 2026. In the Marshall Islands, 156 positive cases were recorded, with 501 specimens tested. Samoa reported 64 new cases, while Vanuatu declared a dengue outbreak on Malekula Island. Tonga saw 137 influenza-like illness cases, with 67 SARI patients hospitalized. Vector control and surveillance measures are ongoing in affected areas.
news.content_zh: 截至2026年10月20日,登革病毒 暴发及相关疾病警报在太平洋多个地区被报告。在马绍尔群岛,记录了156例阳性病例,共检测了501份样本。萨摩亚报告了64例新病例,而瓦努阿图在马勒库拉岛宣布出现登革热暴发。汤加出现了137例流感样病例,其中67例重症急性呼吸道感染(SARI)患者住院治疗。媒介控制及监测措施正在受影响地区持续进行。
news.summary_zh: 截至2026年10月20日,登革病毒 暴发及相关疾病警报在太平洋多个地区被报告。在马绍尔群岛,记录了156例阳性病例,共检测了501份样本。萨摩亚报告了64例新病例,而瓦努阿图在马勒库拉岛宣布出现登革热暴发。汤加出现了137例流感样病例,其中67例重症急性呼吸道感染(SARI)患者住院治疗。媒介控制及监测措施正在受影响地区持续进行。

analysis_zh.location_and_population: 马绍尔群岛、埃贝伊、马朱罗、萨摩亚、瓦努阿图、新喀里多尼亚、新西兰、汤加、密克罗尼西亚联邦。
analysis_zh.event: 登革病毒 暴发及相关疾病警报。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 501 specimens tested, 156 positive cases (Majuro 124, Ebeye 32), 13 cumulative hospitalizations, 5.4 per 1,000 attack rate in Majuro, 3.3 per 1,000 in Ebeye, 64 new cases in Samoa, 22 dengue cases in Vanuatu, 137 influenza-like illness cases in Tonga, 156 of 336 tested ILI cases positive for influenza A, 67 SARI patients hospitalized, 3 deaths among SARI cases.
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 马绍尔群岛、萨摩亚、瓦努阿图和汤加对登革热(DENV-1)发出红色警报,萨摩亚对登革热(DENV-1 & DENV-2)发出蓝色警报,正在进行媒介控制及监测,病例调查,媒介控制,社区意识提升,免费登革热检测,麻疹病例数量经专家评审组确认为确诊病例,流感疫情持续,呼吸道疾病仍具有显著影响,汤加对甲型流感发出红色警报。

One of the most stable segments of the U.S. economy, pest management professionals play a critical role in protecting the public’s health, food and property, providing valuable integrated pest management services to both residential and commercial customers. As the leading monthly trade publication serving this dynamic marketplace, PCT magazine is the industry’s "go-to" source for news and product information.

NPMA Announces 2027 Wildlife Expo Program The program for the 2027 Wildlife Expo, taking place Feb. 9-11 at the DoubleTree by Hilton Orlando at SeaWorld in Orlando, Fla., is now available and features sessions focused on technical skills, business operations, safety and the latest approaches to wildlife management. Certus Acquires Choice Pest Management of Fort Pierce, Fla. Choice will join Certus' pest control and lawn services brand Purcor at the existing Purcor branch in Stuart, Fla., and service Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties. This acquisition further expands Certus’ footprint in the Southeast Florida market. Titan Pest Pro Examined Service-Call Records to Compare its Biggest Markets The Missouri-based company pulled 12 months of real service-call records, 10,156 calls across 128 towns in both markets, and took a closer look at two major cities in its service area. Thomas Pest Services Adds Danielle Restuccia to Team Restuccia will serve as a technical resource for Thomas Pest Services' field teams while helping strengthen the company's training programs, treatment protocols and operational standards. Frontline Pest Control Opens Three New Locations in Tennessee, Virginia The pest management company announced the opening of three new locations in Clarksville, Tenn., Ruckersville, Va., and Ashland, Va., expanding its footprint in communities throughout those states. PCT Announces AI Virtual Conference If you’re wondering how to jump into this next generation of business tools, make plans to attend PCT's November virtual conference "Smarter Service: How AI Can Boost Your Business Today." WellTech Pest Solutions Aims to Take the Sting Out of Breast Cancer WellTech will donate proceeds from all stinging pest jobs completed during October to support breast cancer research, patient care and related services at Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa. News India International Entertainment Cricket Sports Business Videos Videos Photos Local News Bengaluru New Delhi Mumbai Chennai Kolkata Pune Salem Belgaum Ahmedabad Hyderabad Mangalore Elections Upcoming Elections Tamil Nadu Assembly Elections Kerala Assembly Elections West Bengal Assembly Elections Assam Assembly Elections Puducherry Assembly Elections Loksabha Elections Politicians Political Parties Commodity Price Vegetables Price Flowers Price Fruits Price Chicken Price Mutton Price Fish Price Egg Price Weather AQI Lottery Results Prayer Timings Temples in India Quotes Power Cut Dam Water Level Tamil Calendar Malayalam Calendar News India International Entertainment Cricket Sports Business Videos City Bengaluru New Delhi Mumbai Chennai Kolkata Pune Salem Belgaum Ahmedabad Hyderabad Mangalore Sports Pro Kabaddi League Cricket Football Photos Astro Services Movies Bollywood Hollywood Tamil Telugu Malayalam Kannada Television Photo Gallery Lifestyle Health Beauty Cookery Horoscope Festivals Google Doodle Productivity Auto Car News Bike News Reviews How-To Photos EMI Calculator Offbeat Explore Cars Gadgets Mobiles Reviews Photo Gallery Latest Mobiles Upcoming Mobiles Phone Finder Money Quiz Home / Chennai Qdenga Dengue Vaccine: Why Tamil Nadu’s Kadayanallur Pilot Could Be A Turning Point Chennai oi-Prakash KL By Oneindia Desk Published: Monday, October 19, 2026, 12:14 [IST] Add as a preferred source on Google For years, the fight against dengue in India has largely followed the same playbook - control mosquitoes, prevent breeding, identify cases early and treat patients. A new pilot programme in Tamil Nadu is now testing whether vaccination can become another important part of that strategy. Kadayanallur in Tenkasi district has been selected for the pilot, marking an important step in India's efforts to explore dengue vaccination on the ground. AI Summary AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors A dengue vaccination pilot is underway in Kadayanallur, Tamil Nadu, testing the Japanese-developed Qdenga vaccine, approved for ages 4-60 in India, to evaluate its contribution to dengue prevention alongside existing strategies. The choice of Kadayanallur is not accidental. The town has reported a high incidence of dengue, making it a useful setting to study how vaccination works in a population that regularly faces the disease, according to a report in The Hindu. But the exercise will involve more than simply giving people the vaccine. Health officials will also have to track how many eligible residents take the doses, whether they return for the second shot, any side effects and, most importantly, whether dengue cases come down over time. What is the vaccine being used in Tamil Nadu? The vaccine being used in the Kadayanallur programme is Qdenga, developed by Japanese pharmaceutical company Takeda. Qdenga is a live-attenuated, tetravalent dengue vaccine. Put simply, it uses weakened forms of the dengue virus to train the immune system and is designed to provide protection against all four known dengue virus serotypes - DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4. India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation approved Qdenga in July 2026 for people between four and 60 years of age. Also Read Tamil Music Composer Deva Dies At 75; Thenisai Thendral’ Was Known For Baashha, Annamalai The vaccination schedule involves two doses, with the second dose given three months after the first. This is not India's indigenous dengue vaccine The Tamil Nadu programme should not be confused with India's own dengue vaccine candidate. DengiAll, developed by Panacea Biotec in collaboration with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), is a separate vaccine. It entered Phase III clinical trials in August 2024, with 10,335 participants across 19 sites. DengiAll uses dengue virus strains licensed from the US National Institutes of Health (NIH). So, while both vaccines are aimed at tackling dengue, the vaccine being evaluated in the Kadayanallur pilot is the Japan-developed Qdenga. Why is dengue vaccination important? Dengue remains a recurring public health problem in India, particularly during periods when mosquito breeding conditions become favourable. The disease is mainly spread through the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes. For many patients, it causes high fever, severe headache, muscle and joint pain, nausea and other symptoms. In more serious cases, dengue can lead to bleeding, plasma leakage, shock and organ complications. Recommended For You Regime Change Only Through Elections, Not Soros: Kiren Rijiju Warns Of Bangladesh, France-Like Unrest In India Rainfall, temperature, urban growth and stagnant water can all influence the spread of the disease. This makes dengue control difficult because eliminating mosquito breeding sites and protecting people from mosquito bites require sustained efforts. A vaccine, if shown to work effectively in the real-world Indian setting, could give health authorities another weapon in that fight. What will the Tamil Nadu pilot actually tell us? The number of people vaccinated will be only one part of the story. Authorities will need to look at how many people complete the two-dose schedule, what adverse events are reported and whether there is any change in laboratory-confirmed dengue infections. You May Also Like Anirudh Ravichander-Kavya Maran Wedding: Family Invites Vijay, Stalin, Greece Ceremony Planned For 11 November Hospitalisations will also be important. So will the overall cost of running a vaccination programme and whether the benefits justify expanding it to other dengue-prone areas. According to the launch report, two ICMR scientists will study the impact of vaccination in Kadayanallur. The findings could therefore have implications beyond one town in Tenkasi. If the programme produces encouraging results, dengue vaccination could gradually become part of a broader prevention strategy in India - alongside mosquito control and early treatment, rather than replacing them. analysis.brief_en: A dengue vaccination pilot using the Qdenga vaccine is underway in Kadayanallur, Tamil Nadu, India, as part of efforts to explore new prevention strategies. The programme, reported by Oneindia, is being reviewed by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and aims to assess the vaccine's effectiveness in reducing dengue cases in a high-incidence area. The vaccine, developed by Japanese pharmaceutical company Takeda, is approved for ages 4-60 in India and is a live-attenuated, tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue serotypes (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, DENV-4). Health officials will monitor vaccine uptake, adverse events, and changes in laboratory-confirmed dengue infections. The findings could have implications beyond Kadayanallur, potentially shaping broader dengue prevention strategies in India. The pilot is part of a larger effort to integrate vaccination into public health measures against dengue, which remains a recurring issue in the region due to factors like rainfall, temperature, and urban growth.

news.content_zh: 一项使用 Qdenga 疫苗 的登革热 疫苗接种 试点项目正在印度泰米尔纳德邦的卡达亚纳卢尔进行,作为探索新预防策略的一部分。据 Oneindia 报道,该项目由印度医学研究委员会(ICMR)进行评估,旨在评估 疫苗 在高 发病率 区域减少登革热病例的效果。该 疫苗 由日本制药公司 Takeda 开发,已在印度获批用于 4-60 岁人群,是一种活病毒、四价 疫苗,旨在保护所有四种登革病毒血清型(DENV-1、DENV-2、DENV-3、DENV-4)。卫生官员将监测 疫苗 接种率、不良事件以及实验室确认的登革热感染变化。这些发现可能不仅影响卡达亚纳卢尔,还可能影响印度更广泛的登革热预防策略。该试点项目包括两剂接种,第二剂在第一剂接种后三个月进行,且不是印度本土的登革热 疫苗 候选疫苗 DengiAll。该试点项目是更大努力的一部分,旨在将 疫苗接种 整合到印度针对登革热的公共卫生措施中,因为该地区由于降雨、温度和城市化等因素,登革热问题反复出现。

analysis_zh.time: 该试点项目于 2026 年 10 月 19 日在泰米尔纳德邦的卡达亚纳卢尔进行,第二剂计划在第一剂接种后三个月进行。活动日期未明确说明,但该项目仍在进行中。
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 该试点项目在印度泰米尔纳德邦 Tenkasi 县的卡达亚纳卢尔镇进行。该项目涉及一个经常面临登革热的群体,因为该地区登革病毒 发病率 率较高。

OffOn Stream on As dengue continues to rise in Florida, some are worried about underreporting of cases At least 190 cases of locally acquired dengue have been confirmed in 6 counties. ByMary Kekatos September 30, 2026, 3:00 PM Share As cases of dengue fever continue to rise in Florida, public health specialists are worried the true number of infections may be greater. For the week ending Sept. 19, at least 190 cases of locally acquired dengue have been confirmed in the state, an increase of 38 cases from the week before, according to data from the Florida Department of Health (DOH). Hillsborough County, which includes Tampa, is reporting the highest number of cases at 170 followed by Miami-Dade, Orange, Palm Beach, Pasco and Pinellas counties, DOH data shows. Related What to know about dengue fever as Florida reports 1st death and cases rise "There's evidence of local transmission of dengue in several counties in Florida," Natalie Dean, an associate professor of biostatistics and informatics at Emory University's Rollins School of Public Health, told ABC News. "Dengue is not endemic to the United States. That means that it doesn't typically cause local transmission." She added, "There can be occasional outbreaks in the U.S. but this one is notable for its size." Last week, DOH reported the state's first death from dengue fever this year but did not provide any details about the patient including name, age, sex or residence. Close-up of a mosquito biting human skin. Joao Paulo Burini/Getty Images Three counties -- Hillsborough, Pasco and Pinellas -- declared local states of emergency last week. These allow local governments to waive normal procedures, access emergency resources and strengthen efforts to control mosquito populations. Pinellas County crews have been going door to door and spraying areas with high mosquito presence, according to local ABC News affiliate WFTS. "I don't recall a [period] of time when it's been this high in such a sort of concentrated area before," Cameron Wolfe, an infectious diseases specialist and a professor of medicine at Duke University School of Medicine, told ABC News. Wolfe said there may be an underestimate of the true number of cases in Florida. Cases of dengue can be mild, and people may recover on their own or never be tested. Because dengue can resemble a flu-like illness, patients may never suspect the source of their infection. Additionally, he said that reporting of confirmed cases to either local state departments or the CDC can lag. Popular Reads 'Dancing with the Stars' season 35: See who is eliminated 21 hours ago North Korea threatens to restart propaganda broadcasts, deploy more weapons at border Oct 19 Fisherman, 71, attacked and killed by 12-foot alligator alongside Florida lake Oct 17 "For every case that we know, there's going to be a bunch that we never find out about," Wolfe said. Related Increased risk of dengue virus infections in the US: CDC Dean added that people can be infected with dengue multiple times over the course of their life, but it's usually the second or later infection that is more severe, leading to further underreporting. "I always think of like the top of an iceberg," Dean said. "We're only capturing some of the some of the cases." The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) told ABC News in a statement on Tuesday that the agency is "closely tracking dengue activity" and the "unprecedented" number of cases in the Tampa area. The CDC also said they've provided $800,000 in emergency funds to help with the response. "Because the types of mosquitoes that spread dengue, Aedes aegypti, are common throughout many areas of the United States, continued local spread of dengue is possible," the CDC statement said. "The best way to prevent dengue is to protect yourself from mosquito bites by using EPA-registered insect repellant, wearing loose fitting clothes, and controlling mosquitoes in and around your home, such as dumping water." Related Dengue fever cases rise to 6,800 in US amid 2 new infections in Los Angeles: CDC Some research has shown that climate change could be expanding the geographic range and severity of dengue fever. Rising global temperature coupled with more rainfall and humidity -- leading to standing water pools that serve as breeding grounds for mosquitoes -- could increase the number of cases. "Global warming and climate change, in fact, leave places like Florida more wet and more capable of housing these mosquito vectors, so I wouldn't be surprised if this becomes a little more of a perpetual thing," Wolfe said. ABC News' Youri Benadjaoud contributed to this report. OffOn Stream on As dengue continues to rise in Florida, some are worried about underreporting of cases At least 190 cases of locally acquired dengue have been confirmed in 6 counties. ByMary Kekatos September 30, 2026, 3:00 PM Share As cases of dengue fever continue to rise in Florida, public health specialists are worried the true number of infections may be greater. For the week ending Sept. 19, at least 190 cases of locally acquired dengue have been confirmed in the state, an increase of 38 cases from the week before, according to data from the Florida Department of Health (DOH). Hillsborough County, which includes Tampa, is reporting the highest number of cases at 170 followed by Miami-Dade, Orange, Palm Beach, Pasco and Pinellas counties, DOH data shows. Related What to know about dengue fever as Florida reports 1st death and cases rise "There's evidence of local transmission of dengue in several counties in Florida," Natalie Dean, an associate professor of biostatistics and informatics at Emory University's Rollins School of Public Health, told ABC News. "Dengue is not endemic to the United States. That means that it doesn't typically cause local transmission." She added, "There can be occasional outbreaks in the U.S. but this one is notable for its size." Last week, DOH reported the state's first death from dengue fever this year but did not provide any details about the patient including name, age, sex or residence. Close-up of a mosquito biting human skin. Joao Paulo Burini/Getty Images Three counties -- Hillsborough, Pasco and Pinellas -- declared local states of emergency last week. These allow local governments to waive normal procedures, access emergency resources and strengthen efforts to control mosquito populations. Pinellas County crews have been going door to door and spraying areas with high mosquito presence, according to local ABC News affiliate WFTS. "I don't recall a [period] of time when it's been this high in such a sort of concentrated area before," Cameron Wolfe, an infectious diseases specialist and a professor of medicine at Duke University School of Medicine, told ABC News. Wolfe said there may be an underestimate of the true number of cases in Florida. Cases of dengue can be mild, and people may recover on their own or never be tested. Because dengue can resemble a flu-like illness, patients may never suspect the source of their infection. Additionally, he said that reporting of confirmed cases to either local state departments or the CDC can lag. Popular Reads 'Dancing with the Stars' season 35: See who is eliminated 21 hours ago North Korea threatens to restart propaganda broadcasts, deploy more weapons at border Oct 19 Fisherman, 71, attacked and killed by 12-foot alligator alongside Florida lake Oct 17 "For every case that we know, there's going to be a bunch that we never find out about," Wolfe said. Related Increased risk of dengue virus infections in the US: CDC Dean added that people can be infected with dengue multiple times over the course of their life, but it's usually the second or later infection that is more severe, leading to further underreporting. "I always think of like the top of an iceberg," Dean said. "We're only capturing some of the some of the cases." The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) told ABC News in a statement on Tuesday that the agency is "closely tracking dengue activity" and the "unprecedented" number of cases in the Tampa area. The CDC also said they've provided $800,000 in emergency funds to help with the response. "Because the types of mosquitoes that spread dengue, Aedes aegypti, are common throughout many areas of the United States, continued local spread of dengue is possible," the CDC statement said. "The best way to prevent dengue is to protect yourself from mosquito bites by using EPA-registered insect repellant, wearing loose fitting clothes, and controlling mosquitoes in and around your home, such as dumping water." Related Dengue fever cases rise to 6,800 in US amid 2 new infections in Los Angeles: CDC Some research has shown that climate change could be expanding the geographic range and severity of dengue fever. Rising global temperature coupled with more rainfall and humidity -- leading to standing water pools that serve as breeding grounds for mosquitoes -- could increase the number of cases. "Global warming and climate change, in fact, leave places like Florida more wet and more capable of housing these mosquito vectors, so I wouldn't be surprised if this becomes a little more of a perpetual thing," Wolfe said. ABC News' Youri Benadjaoud contributed to this report. When surveillance officers in Amran governorate noticed a surge of suspected dengue in Harf Sufyan district in early September 2023, a rapid investigation team was dispatched within days. The resulting case-control study, published in BMC Infectious Diseases, confirms the outbreak and pinpoints two strikingly simple risk factors: wearing short-sleeved clothing and working outdoors. The investigation began on September 5, 2023, just one day after the surveillance officer in Amran governorate reported an increased number of suspected dengue fever cases in Harf Sufyan. A joint team from Yemen’s electronic Integrated Disease Early Warning System, known as eIDEWS, and the Rapid Response program traveled to the district to confirm whether an outbreak existed, determine its risk factors, and recommend control measures. Their work offers a technical template for outbreak response in one of the world’s most challenging public health environments. Discover more Study Biology Get Health Tips Donate to Research The team conducted a descriptive case-control study in Harf Sufyan from September 5 to October 29, 2023, using a 1:2 matching ratio. Cases were defined according to the standard World Health Organization case definition of dengue fever, while controls were any person living in the same area whose house was adjacent to the homes of cases and who had not developed dengue fever. Data were collected on individual, environmental, and behavioral risk factors. Attack rates, odds ratios, and confidence intervals were calculated, with a p-value below 0.05 considered statistically significant. Check Symptoms Discover more Check Symptoms Buy Maps Read History Learn Arabic Laboratory confirmation strengthened the descriptive picture. A total of 34 patients tested positive for dengue fever IgM antibodies, and 68 controls were enrolled. Males made up 58 percent of the confirmed cases, and 43 percent were younger than 30 years of age. The overall attack rate was 0.9 per 100 of the population. The first case fell in epidemiological week 37 of 2023, and the outbreak reached its peak in week 39, a compressed epidemic curve typical of explosive dengue transmission in a susceptible population. Multivariate analysis cut through the noise of dozens of candidate exposures. Only two factors remained significantly associated with dengue infection after adjustment: wearing shorts and T-shirts, which carried an odds ratio of 17 with a confidence interval of 4.8 to 60.1, and working, which carried an odds ratio of 23 with a confidence interval of 2.9 to 33.2. In practical terms, people who wore short-sleeved clothing were roughly 17 times more likely to be infected, and those who worked were roughly 23 times more likely, than their neighbors who did not share those exposures. Check Symptoms The biological logic behind these findings is straightforward. Dengue virus is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, principally Aedes aegypti, which bite during daytime hours and preferentially attack exposed skin. Short sleeves and T-shirts leave forearms and legs uncovered, maximizing the surface area available to a day-biting vector. Outdoor work places people in the open during the very hours when Aedes aegypti is most active, multiplying the number of potential infective bites. In Harf Sufyan, where many residents labor in fields and open-air workplaces, the combination of exposed skin and occupational daytime presence created ideal conditions for rapid viral amplification. The demographic profile of the outbreak adds context. With males comprising a majority of cases and nearly half of patients under 30, the epidemic pattern mirrors the working-age structure of the exposed population rather than any special vulnerability of children or the elderly. An attack rate of 0.9 per 100 may sound modest, but in a district with limited health infrastructure, even a small proportion of clinically ill patients can overwhelm primary care facilities, particularly when dengue can progress to severe dengue, dengue hemorrhagic fever, or dengue shock syndrome in a minority of infections. Discover more Track Outbreaks Find Treatments infection infections Infectious Diseases The authors conclude that dengue fever is emerging as an important disease in Harf Sufyan district of Amran governorate. Occupational exposure and wearing short-sleeved clothing were identified as the primary significant risk factors, a finding with immediate operational value. Because the protective behavior is as simple as covering more skin, the study recommends increasing community awareness about dengue infection, its mode of transmission, and control measures, along with the use of protective clothing. Such messaging can be delivered through existing community networks without costly equipment or pharmaceutical intervention. Check Symptoms The broader significance of the study extends beyond a single district. Yemen’s health system has been battered by years of conflict, and the eIDEWS and Rapid Response infrastructure demonstrated here shows that even under strain, rapid outbreak confirmation and analytic epidemiology remain feasible. The case-control design, executed with a 1:2 ratio and standard WHO case definitions, produced actionable odds ratios within weeks of the initial alert. For other districts in the Eastern Mediterranean Region where dengue is expanding, the Yemeni experience suggests that vector-borne risk assessment should focus on daytime occupational exposure and clothing coverage as first-line behavioral targets. For a virus with no specific antiviral treatment and a vaccine landscape still uneven in endemic countries, behavioral prevention remains the backbone of dengue control. The Harf Sufyan outbreak, confirmed through 34 IgM-positive cases and dissected through multivariate analysis, distilled that backbone into two measurable exposures. As dengue continues its global expansion into new territories, the lesson from northern Yemen is that the fight against the virus can begin with something as ordinary as a long-sleeved shirt and as fundamental as recognizing who, in a community, faces the greatest daytime exposure to the mosquitoes that carry it. news.source_body_en: A dengue fever outbreak in Harf Sufyan district, Amran governorate, Yemen, was confirmed through a case-control study published in BMC Infectious Diseases. The outbreak, which peaked in epidemiological week 39 of 2023, was linked to two key risk factors: wearing short-sleeved clothing and working outdoors. These exposures increased the likelihood of infection by 17 and 23 times, respectively, compared to individuals not sharing these behaviors. The study highlights the importance of behavioral prevention strategies, such as using protective clothing, in dengue control. With an attack rate of 0.9 per 100, the outbreak could strain local health infrastructure, especially as dengue can progress to severe forms like dengue hemorrhagic fever or dengue shock syndrome. The findings suggest that public health efforts should focus on daytime occupational exposure and clothing coverage as first-line behavioral targets in regions with expanding dengue transmission.
news.content_zh: 一项发表在《BMC Infectious Diseases》上的病例对照研究确认了也门Amran省Harf Sufyan区的一次登革热暴发。此次暴发在2023年流行病学第39周达到高峰,与两个关键风险因素相关:穿着短袖衣物和户外工作。与不具有这些行为的人相比,这些暴露因素分别使感染风险增加了17倍和23倍。该研究强调了行为预防策略在登革热控制中的重要性,例如使用防护性衣物。此次暴发的发病率是0.9/100,可能对当地卫生基础设施造成压力,尤其是在登革热可能发展为重症登革热或登革热休克综合征的情况下。研究结果表明,在登革热暴发范围扩大的地区,公共卫生努力应将白天职业暴露和衣物覆盖作为首要的行为干预目标。
